builder_plan.scenario: You already need task-specific training and want to reduce its memory or compute cost.
builder_plan.change: Change only the training technique on a small controlled run after checking prerequisites.
builder_plan.baseline: Your current training recipe with the same model, data split, and evaluation.
steps: Locate the paper's implementation and check its license, model support, data needs, and hardware requirements. Stop here if you cannot obtain the required artifacts.
Save a small set of representative product tasks and expected outcomes. Keep evaluation tasks out of any training or tuning, and choose quality and cost limits before running.
Run the baseline and the proposed change on identical inputs. Keep other settings fixed and repeat paired runs to expose variation.
Save per-task outputs, failures, timings, and all usage costs. Review regressions before expanding the test.
builder_plan.measure: Held-out quality, peak memory, training time, and full compute cost to the target quality.
builder_plan.decision: Keep the change only if it meets your preselected quality and latency limits and improves the metric you care about after setup and operating costs. Otherwise retain the baseline. This is an exploration plan, not a validated recommendation.

title: Text-Conditioned Low-Rank Adaptation of Time-Series Foundation Models for Multimodal Forecasting
summary: It replaces input-level or representation-level text fusion in multimodal forecasting by generating instance-specific LoRA updates from encoded text while keeping the time-series backbone and text encoder frozen, exactly recovering the frozen model when no context is present. The cost is training and maintaining a hypernetwork that maps text embeddings to low-rank weight deltas, plus the engineering overhead of curating aligned text context per forecast instance; inference overhead is a single text encoding and LoRA merge. It can fail when text context is unavailable, noisy, or misaligned with the series, when the text distribution shifts from training, or when the target workload lacks the textual side information the benchmark assumes.
rationale: The method requires only training a small LoRA-generator on top of frozen backbones, which fits a single 24 GB GPU, but the gains are validated on one benchmark and only pay off when forecast-relevant text context actually exists in the workload.
technique: Text-conditioned LoRA generation for time-series foundation models

claims.statement: It replaces input-level or representation-level text fusion in multimodal forecasting by generating instance-specific LoRA updates from encoded text while keeping the time-series backbone and text encoder frozen, exactly recovering the frozen model when no context is present. The cost is training and maintaining a hypernetwork that maps text embeddings to low-rank weight deltas, plus the engineering overhead of curating aligned text context per forecast instance; inference overhead is a single text encoding and LoRA merge. It can fail when text context is unavailable, noisy, or misaligned with the series, when the text distribution shifts from training, or when the target workload lacks the textual side information the benchmark assumes.

On Time-MMD across nine domains and three TSFM architectures, C2LoRA-TS achieves lower aggregate forecasting error than frozen-TSFM and Static LoRA baselines for every architecture and seed; a fixed global context degrades performance.
